title: The going rate for a second passport is $200,000
description: Five Caribbean countries agreed not to sell citizenship below two hundred thousand dollars. Europe no longer sells the passport itself, only residency and a place in the queue. Here is what the money actually buys, and who it pays.

scenes.narration: A second passport has a price, and it is publicly listed.
scenes.imagePrompt: Empty white sand Caribbean beach at midday, calm turquoise shallows, a single wooden sun lounger with a folded white towel standing under a palm, hard palm-frond shadows striping the sand across the foreground, deep blue sky, no people

scenes.narration: Five Caribbean countries agreed a floor. Below two hundred thousand dollars, nobody sells.
scenes.imagePrompt: Colonial government building on a Caribbean island in bright midday sun, pale stone facade with green louvred shutters and a columned portico, tall palms throwing hard shadows across the white wall, deep blue sky filling the upper frame, empty street in front

scenes.narration: You do not move there. You do not learn the language. You wire the money.
scenes.imagePrompt: Interior of a sunlit colonial bank hall on a Caribbean island at midday, polished marble floor and a long dark wooden counter running down one side, tall louvred shutters throwing hard bars of light across the floor, a ceiling fan overhead, deep shadow in the corners, everything in crisp sharp focus from foreground to background, deep depth of field, no blur, no people

scenes.narration: Approval takes about four months. Then the document arrives by courier.
scenes.imagePrompt: Sealed courier envelope with a red wax seal lying on a sunlit teak table on a Caribbean terrace, photographed from a low raking angle so the face of the envelope is turned away from camera and only its thick edge and seal catch the light, hard palm-frond shadows striping the table, sharply rendered turquoise sea and white sand behind it, everything in crisp sharp focus from front to back, deep depth of field, no blur

scenes.narration: It opens roughly a hundred and fifty countries without a visa application.
scenes.imagePrompt: Bright tropical airport departure hall at midday, a tall glass wall flooded with sunlight looking out onto palms and a sunlit apron under a clear blue sky, rows of empty seats sitting in deep shade in the foreground, hard bars of light falling across the polished floor

scenes.narration: Europe stopped selling the passport itself. Now it sells residency, and residency is only a place in the queue.
scenes.imagePrompt: Narrow sunlit limestone street in a Mediterranean island capital at midday, honey-coloured stone buildings with traditional enclosed wooden balconies painted deep green, deep shadow filling the lower half of the street, a bright wedge of blue sea visible at the far end, everything in crisp sharp focus from foreground to background, deep depth of field, no blur, no people

scenes.narration: For some of the selling countries, this is a third of government revenue.
scenes.imagePrompt: Elevated midday view over a small Caribbean island capital seen from a shaded hilltop, dark green foliage framing the top of the frame, pastel houses with red tin roofs stepping down the hillside to a turquoise harbour, moored sailing boats along a stone quay below, deep blue sea stretching to the horizon, everything in crisp sharp focus from foreground to background, deep depth of field, no blur, no people

scenes.narration: So citizenship is not always something you are born into. Sometimes it is just a line on a price list.
scenes.imagePrompt: Empty white sand Caribbean beach at midday seen from under a palm, the dark trunk and fronds framing the top of the frame in deep shadow, turquoise sea with a distant sailing boat, hard shadows falling across the sand in the foreground
